title: HATF Precision Loss for Five-Round Ascon
summary: Second-order HATF is less precise for five-round than four-round Ascon; determine whether added HATF complexity and extra independence assumptions are the main cause.

formal_statement.body: For second-order HATF analyses of four-round and five-round Ascon, validate or refute the conjecture that the loss of precision in the five-round setting is caused mainly by the greater complexity of the HATF system, which entails independence assumptions for more intermediate-state bits and therefore makes those assumptions more likely to fail.

scope.domain: Higher-order differential-linear cryptanalysis of reduced-round Ascon using second-order HATF.
assumptions: Independence assumptions for intermediate-state bits in the HATF system.
parameters: Analysis order: fixed to second order
Ascon round count: comparison between four-round and five-round settings
scope.unresolved_remainder: Validate or refute whether increased HATF complexity and the resulting additional independence assumptions are the main cause of the five-round precision loss.

citations.label: Revisiting Higher-Order Differential-Linear Attacks from an Algebraic Perspective

progress.summary: The source reports reduced second-order HATF precision for five-round versus four-round Ascon and explicitly conjectures that greater system complexity and more independence assumptions are mainly responsible.
citation_labels: Kai Hu et al., Revisiting Higher-Order Differential-Linear Attacks from an Algebraic Perspective
